title: Wellington, Vanguard, and Blackstone Announce the Launch of Two Investment Solutions, Simplifying Access to Public and Private Markets
summary: Press releases, portfolio company news, and timely updates on our business.
body_text: Wellington, Vanguard, and Blackstone Announce the Launch of Two Investment Solutions, Simplifying Access to Public and Private Markets July 22, 2026 Funds available at launch through Bank of America wealth management platforms BOSTON, VALLEY FORGE, AND NEW YORK, July 22, 2026 – Wellington Management (“Wellington”), Vanguard, and Blackstone (NYSE: BX) today announced the launch of two new investment solutions created as part of their recently formed strategic alliance and designed to give eligible investors simplified access to professionally managed portfolios that combine public and private markets. WVB All Markets Fund, a multi-asset solution for investors who want to simplify the integration of public and private markets. The fund will integrate Wellington’s expertise in active public equities, Vanguard’s strengths in active fixed income and index strategies, with exposure to Blackstone’s leading perpetual private markets platform. The fund will trade under the tickers WVBIX, WVBAX, and WVBMX. WVB Blackstone All Privates Fund, a professionally managed solution providing a simple access point to Blackstone’s leading perpetual private markets platform, including private equity, private infrastructure, private real estate, and private credit in a single allocation. The new closed-end funds will be available at launch to Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank clients, providing advisors on one of the industry’s leading wealth management platforms with access to the first solutions from the strategic alliance. The alliance also anticipates broad participation and adoption from the RIA community, and will explore additional distribution opportunities across the wealth ecosystem over time. The solutions aim to help advisors build more diversified portfolios for high-net-worth and mass-affluent clients in a simplified investment framework. The funds are intended to help advisors construct long-term portfolios that seek strong performance, long-term growth, and broad portfolio diversification. A Powerful Alliance of Investment Leaders The WVB All Markets Fund and WVB Blackstone All Privates Fund bring together: Wellington’s nearly 100-year heritage of active management, fundamental research, and multi-asset allocation expertise; Vanguard’s 50-year legacy of delivering high-performing active strategies and index funds[ 1 ] with a relentless focus on cost efficiency and investor outcomes; and Blackstone’s 40-year track record of cycle-tested performance and leadership position as the world’s largest alternative asset manager and number one provider of private markets solutions for individuals. Together, the firms are uniquely positioned to deliver integrated investment solutions that were historically available primarily to large institutions. To expand access to their collective strengths, Wellington, Vanguard, and Blackstone are actively exploring additional product structures to support retirement savers, financial advisors, and individual investors. Mark Sutterlin, Head of Alternative Investments, Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank, said: “Our clients are increasingly seeking broader access to private markets and for thoughtful ways to implement these strategies over time. Our scale and integrated platforms are expanding access to differentiated investment opportunities that can support more resilient long-term portfolios.” Jean M. Hynes, CEO and Managing Partner, Wellington Management, said: “The launch of the WVB All Markets and WVB Blackstone All Privates Funds reflects the strength of our strategic alliance with Vanguard and Blackstone. By combining our deep active management and asset allocation capabilities with Vanguard’s scale and expertise in fixed income and indexing and Blackstone’s leadership in private markets, we are delivering thoughtfully constructed solutions designed to meet investors’ evolving needs. We are particularly pleased to introduce these funds initially through the powerful Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank platforms.” Greg Davis, President and CIO of Vanguard, said: “For five decades, Vanguard has worked to improve investor outcomes through disciplined active management, low-cost index strategies, and a client-focused approach. Through this collaboration with Wellington and Blackstone, we are extending that mission into integrated public and private market solutions. Launching these funds with Bank of America Private Bank and Merrill is an important first step in expanding access to those solutions.” Jon Gray, President and COO of Blackstone, said: “Blackstone has delivered performance in private markets for individuals for more than two decades, helping them access the premium returns, lower volatility, and diversification that private markets can provide. These new solutions bring together the performance and scale of Blackstone’s private markets platform with the exceptional strengths of Wellington and Vanguard, creating simple and comprehensive access for advisors and their clients to help build long-term wealth.” [ 1 ] For the 10-year period ending June 30, 2026, 77% of Vanguard funds outperformed the average return of their peer group, or 260 of 336 Vanguard funds. body_text: 7/9/2026 Polaris and Minnesota 4-H Expand Youth ATV Safety Education Through a Fun Interactive Adventure Digital Trailblazers Experience Introduces Foundational ATV Safety Learning and Strengthens Long-standing Partnership Minneapolis, MN [July 09, 2026] – Polaris in partnership with Minnesota 4-H , is expanding its youth ATV safety education with the launch of a new interactive safety adventure available on CLOVER , 4-H’s online learning platform. At its core, Trailblazers are built around a simple idea: learning safety should be as engaging and rewarding as the adventures young riders dream about having. The ATV Adventure Academy: Trailblazers experience introduces youth to foundational safe-riding practices in an engaging, trail-themed digital environment to make learning fun while sparking interest in outdoor adventure and future riding experiences. Built around interactive choices, animated sequences, and a trail map with progressive levels, the Trailblazers safety adventure immerses youth in scenarios that help them explore responsible riding practices, including selecting proper gear, making safer decisions, and recognizing trail signs. With youth involved in the creation of the experience from the start, it’s designed for ease and engagement. “We provided feedback on the flow of the experience and age-appropriate play and questions,” said Minnesota 4-H ATV Safety Ambassador, Rebecca Anderson, “I’ve personally learned that ATV safety is something that needs to be taught, not assumed. It’s important to me that other youth learn ATV safety as well, so I wanted to help make it fun because when kids enjoy it, they actually remember it. That’s how you build good habits early.” While the content is geared towards youth ages 10-13, the adventure is open to anyone curious about ATV safety and serves as an accessible starting point before moving onto Minnesota 4-H’s hands-on ATV Safety programming or other state-certified trainings and ASI (ATV Safety Institute) certifications. “Trailblazers is designed to meet youth riders at the beginning of their safety journey and help build their confidence through engaging, scenario-based learning,” said Korinne Caldwell, Polaris Employee Health and Safety Manager, ASI/ATV Instructor and ROHVA Certified Instructor. “By introducing foundational safety principles early, and in ways that reflect real riding situations, we’re helping young riders develop the habits they need to ride responsibly and safely. When youth understand these skills, they’re better equipped to enjoy the freedom and adventure of being outdoors with confidence. That’s why Polaris is committed to advancing youth rider safety, and why Trailblazers plays such an important role in that mission.” The launch of this safety adventure marks the latest milestone in the long-standing collaboration between Polaris and Minnesota 4-H . Since 2019, the partnership has supported youth ATV and UTV safety education through hands‑on training, safety displays at farm safety events and county and state fairs, and expanded curriculum and volunteer training reaching more than 800,000 youth. Building on this foundation, Polaris and Minnesota 4‑H are sharing resources and learnings to support multi‑state program pilots, including current collaborations with 4‑H partners in Wisconsin and Utah, extending responsible riding education to more youth and families. About University of Minnesota and Minnesota 4-H Minnesota 4-H is the largest youth development program in the state, serving 58,000 youth in the 2024/2025 program year. The program, run by University of Minnesota Extension, is developed using rigorous educational standards and is designed to nurture youth into becoming innovators and leaders. title: Age-appropriate chores for kids: a chore chart that builds executive function skills
summary: Age-appropriate chores for kids, by age, plus how to run a chore chart that builds executive function skills like planning, working memory, and follow-through.
body_text: The chore chart by age Match the job to where your child's executive function actually is, not where you wish it were. A two-year-old can't plan a sequence yet; a ten-year-old is bored by a job with no ownership in it. Use these as a starting menu, then let your child help choose. Ages 2 to 3: one-step jobs, side by side Put toys in a bin Drop dirty clothes in the hamper Hand you groceries to put away Wipe a spill with a cloth At this age the win is simply following a single instruction to completion, alongside you. You're planting the idea that they're a contributor. Ages 4 to 5: two-step jobs, with a picture chart Set the table (napkins, then forks) Feed a pet with a measured scoop Make the bed, roughly Water plants This is where a picture chart earns its keep. Two steps in the right order is real planning for a preschooler. Ages 6 to 7: multi-step jobs they can start solo Pack their own snack and water bottle Sort laundry into lights and darks Clear and wipe the table after dinner Get the backpack ready the night before Task initiation is the focus now. The goal is starting on one cue instead of five reminders. Ages 8 to 9: jobs with a quality bar Load or unload the dishwasher Take out trash and recycling on the right day Vacuum a room Help make a simple meal from a recipe card Add a self-check step. "Recycling on the right day" quietly builds the calendar-awareness that homework planners will later demand. Ages 10 to 11: jobs they manage over time Do their own laundry start to finish Plan and prep one family meal a week Care for a pet's full routine Manage a weekly tidy of their room without prompting These stretch across days, so kids practice holding a goal in mind and monitoring their own progress, the core of long-project stamina. Ages 12 and up: jobs that mirror adult systems Run a grocery sub-list on a budget Manage their own schedule of jobs across the week Do yard work or deeper cleaning tasks Track and complete a recurring responsibility without a chart at all By now the chart itself should be fading. A teen who can run their responsibilities without an external tracker has internalized the executive-function skills you spent a decade building. Four mistakes that turn a chore chart into a battle Doing the planning for them. If you sequence every step, you're exercising your executive function, not theirs. Hand back the thinking. Too many jobs at once. Three consistent jobs beat ten sporadic ones. Overloading the chart guarantees it gets abandoned. Redoing their work in front of them. A wobbly bed made by a five-year-old is a win. Silently remaking it teaches them their effort doesn't count. Never fading the reminders. If you're still cueing every step months in, the chart has become your job. Shrink the prompt on purpose. Frequently asked questions Should chores be tied to allowance? Many families separate the two: some jobs are simply part of belonging to the household, while a few extra paid jobs can teach money skills. If you want to build financial habits alongside responsibility, see our guide to life skills to teach kids at home . What if my child has ADHD or struggles with getting started? Lean harder on the visual chart, shorten the jobs, and make the first cue playful rather than nagging. Our roundup of executive function activities for kids has more that pairs well with a chore routine. My kid just refuses. Now what? Drop the count to one job, do it together for a week, and give them a real choice in which job it is. Ownership beats enforcement almost every time. Where classes fit in Chores build the executive-function foundation. Structured classes give kids another place to practice the same planning-and-follow-through muscles with a teacher who's watching for them. If you want to understand the skill you're building before you build it, start with what executive function is and why it matters , and see how play-based learning builds life skills from a different angle. When you're ready, a live small-group class on Outschool can give your child a low-stakes place to practice organization and independence outside the home. Sources [1] Diamond, A. (2013). Executive Functions. Annual Review of Psychology. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4084861/ [2] American Academy of Pediatrics, HealthyChildren.org. If you’re interested in a well-rounded privacy bundle, encompassing email/phone aliases, spam-call blocking, a password manager, VPN, $1M identity theft insurance, dark web monitoring, and a basic personal data removal service all in one, then Cloaked is the better choice. However, if your main concern is personal data removal from data brokers, Optery is by the better choice. Cloaked does have a personal data removal service capability, but it is not as comprehensive or robust as Optery in this area. As one Redditor said “Although they (Cloaked) also include data removal, I found it to be far less intuitive and the communication (as far as what exactly the status was for removals) compared to Optery, who’s sole focus is to search for and remove your data from brokers.” Another option to consider is to use both services simultaneously, supplementing Cloaked’s well-rounded bundle with Optery’s industry-leading personal data removal service. It also had the highest removal success rate according to Consumer Reports’ testing.” Zachary McAuliffe Senior Writer, CNET 💡 Important Note to Current Customers of Cloaked: Existing Cloaked customers can create a free Optery account and review the results of the free Optery Exposure Report scan to test Cloaked’s performance and double-check Cloaked’s work. Based on our research and testing, Optery finds ~50 exposed profiles for customers of other personal data removal services on average. Executive Summary Best fit for Cloaked: People who want one subscription that bundles email and phone aliases, a password manager, spam call blocking, VPN, identity theft insurance, and a basic personal data removal service all in one subscription. Best fit for Optery: People who want the #1 most effective personal data removal service on the market, or who want to take a “best of breed” approach, selecting the best product on the market for each functional area, e.g. the best VPN, Password Manager, Identity Theft Insurance, Personal Data Removal, etc – all from different “best of breed” vendors. Cloaked Strengths: Broad feature bundle beyond data removal (aliases, Call Guard, dark web and SSN monitoring, $1M identity theft insurance), a straightforward flat-rate family plan, and independently verified security certifications (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27701, PCI DSS v4.0.1). Cloaked Limitations: No ongoing free tier (only a lead-generation “free scan”), no public before-and-after screenshot verification of data broker removals, more limited data broker removal coverage than Optery. Optery Strengths: A genuinely free Free Basic account with screenshots, clearly published plan-by-plan broker counts, most comprehensive and effective data broker removal coverage in the industry, unlimited Custom Removals Requests, Blur Your Home on Google Maps and Apple Maps, and screenshot-based removal verification on paid plans. Flexible billing options: Monthly, Yearly, and the ability to Pause / Resume / Upgrade / Downgrade subscriptions at any time. Also offers a straight-forward family plan, and industry leading security certification (SOC 2 Type 2). Optery Limitations: Does not offer privacy bundle features beyond personal data removal at this time. Who should choose which service: Cloaked can suit someone who wants one subscription for aliases and a light-weight personal data removal function together. Optery fits better for anyone who wants the most comprehensive, effective, and robust personal data removal, with verifiable proof of removal screenshots. The rest of their list is tagged for “Other websites”, e.g. sites like The Cheesecake Factory (huh???) Optery offers completely transparent pricing and feature list on its Pricing page. Subscription plans start at $3.99 / month or $39 per year for 380+ data broker sites, all the way up to $24.99 per month or $249 per year for 950+ data broker sites (or 405 without enabling Expanded Reach ). Reporting cadence Continuous monitoring and Automated scans. Progress is tracked through In-App Dashboard Real Time Reporting viewable through In-App Dashboard with Quarterly Removal Reports (with Before and After Screenshots) for Extended and Ultimate Plans; Free Quarterly Exposure Reports for Free Tier 1. What Cloaked Does Well Cloaked deserves credit on several fronts, based on what its own site and independent coverage confirm. A genuinely bundled privacy suite. Cloaked pairs data broker removal with unlimited email and phone aliases, a password manager, spam call blocking, VPN, dark web and SSN monitoring, and $1 million in identity theft insurance, all in one subscription. For someone who wants a single app rather than several separate tools, that is a real convenience. Simple household pricing. Cloaked’s Family plan covers up to four people for $24.99 per month billed annually, with the full feature set included for everyone on the plan. For a household that wants aliases and light removal together, this is easy to understand. Verified security certifications. Cloaked’s trust page documents ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certification, a completed PCI DSS v4.0.1 audit, and SOC 2 Type 2 compliance. These are checkable credentials, not just marketing language. Included identity theft insurance. Cloaked’s homepage states coverage of up to $1 million in financial losses from identity theft and fraud, included standard rather than sold as an add-on. For users who place a premium on this kind of backstop, this is a real differentiator from removal-only competitors. A large total site directory. Cloaked’s own site-coverage page lists 1,000+ individual sites it monitors and works to remove data from, spanning both data brokers and other companies (retailers, employers, and similar organizations) that may hold a person’s contact information. For users who mainly want a bundled privacy app, aliases for everyday sign-ups, and basic broker cleanup as one part of a bigger toolkit, this may be enough. 2. In the Realm of Personal Data Removal Cloaked Falls Short If your interest is in personal data removal from data brokers, based on Cloaked’s website, several gaps are worth understanding before you subscribe. Coverage numbers vary, and coverage numbers are inflated with a puzzling set of sites. Cloaked’s site-coverage directory, when filtered to the “Data Broker” category specifically, lists 354 sites. The same directory’s total count, across data brokers and “other websites” (mainstream consumer/business sites), is 1,000+, including sites like The Cheesecake Factory and UCLA Health (?). Separately, Cloaked’s enterprise page states data is removed from “400+ data brokers”. Optery covers 950+ data brokers, and doesn’t inflate its list with sites like The Cheesecake Factory and UCLA Health. Cloaked Data Broker Coverage No visible screenshot-based removal verification. Before-and-after screenshots showing that a specific profile was found and later removed are not available. This may not matter to every user, but it is a notable limitation for anyone who wants independent, verifiable evidence instead of relying on a running counter. Optery provides before-and-after screenshot evidence, proving its work in its Removals Reports. The “free scan” is a lead-generation tool, not an ongoing free tier. Cloaked’s homepage free scan asks for a phone number and produces an exposure report, but it’s not a persistent free account with continued monitoring, comparable to a free tier you could use indefinitely without paying. If you want free, ongoing visibility into your exposure, this is a limitation. Optery offers a Free Basic account tier for free self-service removals tools and free ongoing Exposure Reports with screenshots. Regional coverage is limited. Cloaked’s own footer states the service is “currently available in the USA and Canada.” This may not matter for most US-based buyers, but it is worth knowing if you need coverage elsewhere. Optery is currently available in the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and South Africa. 3. Data Broker Coverage Comparison Coverage question Cloaked Optery Public broker list available? Verification and Reporting for Personal Data Removal Verification is the difference between a service telling you it removed your data and showing you it did. Optery’s Exposure Reports show where a person’s profile appears at data broker and people-search sites, using what the company calls “patented view links” so users can see the profile without necessarily contacting the broker directly themselves. Optery adds Removals Reports approximately every 90 days that include before-and-after screenshots which is the only personal data removal service that provides detailed exposure and removal reports, complete with screenshots, to demonstrate the effectiveness of its services. Cloaked’s dashboard, per its help center, shows a running “Total records removed” count, “Days Protected,” and in-progress versus completed broker scans. This gives a user a sense of overall progress, but it is a different kind of evidence than a screenshot showing a specific profile disappearing from a specific site. Optery’s key advantage here is not just that it says removals happened, they also show where profiles were found and, later, screenshot evidence tied to the removal. That is a meaningfully more auditable model for a privacy professional who needs to document that a specific exposure was actually resolved, and it is also easier for an everyday consumer to understand at a glance. 5. Get Started for Free Banking Best Bank Accounts for Small Businesses in 2026: Compare Fees, Features and Choose the Right One By Esha Panda Published on 29 Jul 2026 16 min read The best business bank account is the one that fits how your business actually operates. A freelancer sending a few invoices each month needs something very different from an e-commerce brand processing thousands of transactions or a startup preparing to raise funding. That’s why choosing a business bank account can feel overwhelming. Every provider claims to be the “best,” every comparison ranks them differently, and the fine print on fees often tells a different story than the marketing headline. Instead of looking for a one-size-fits-all winner, it’s better to compare accounts based on your business model, banking needs, and long-term goals. What looks like the “top” pick in one roundup might charge you hidden monthly fees, lock you into minimum balances you can’t realistically maintain, or simply not support the way you actually get paid. This guide skips the generic rankings. Instead, you’ll get a practical, decision-first breakdown of the best business bank accounts in 2026, organized by fees, features, and the specific type of business you’re running, so, you can match an account to your needs instead of guessing. Before you choose a business bank account, make sure your business is set up the right way. Match the account to your transaction volume, business stage, and whether you need physical branches or pure online banking Who This Guide Is For This guide is for you if you fall into one of these groups: You’re a freelancer or solopreneur who needs to separate personal and business income without paying for features you’ll never use You’re a startup owner who needs an account that scales with fundraising, payroll, and investor reporting You’re running an e-commerce business and need integrations with Stripe , Shopify or Amazon, plus tools to track inventory spend separately from marketing spend You run an agency or service business and need to manage client payments, contractor payouts, and tax set-asides without juggling spreadsheets Note: If you’re a side hustler still testing an idea, you can usually start with a no-fee account and upgrade later. If you’re scaling fast, prioritize an account that won’t force a migration once you outgrow it. And if you do business internationally, whether that’s paying overseas contractors or collecting payments from customers abroad, multi-currency support should weigh heavily in your decision. What Is a Business Bank Account (And Why It Matters) You register a business bank account under your company’s legal name and EIN, not your own. It keeps your business income and expenses separate from your personal finances, which matters for both legal protection and tax clarity. How It Works for Small Businesses The flow is straightforward: your business receives income into the account, you pay expenses and vendors out of it, and at tax time, your bookkeeping is clean because every transaction in the account is a business transaction. Compare that to a personal account, where business and personal spending get mixed together and every tax season becomes an exercise in untangling receipts. If your business is structured as an LLC, keeping finances separate isn’t just good practice. Mixing personal and business funds can lead a court to “pierce the corporate veil,” which strips away the liability protection an LLC is supposed to provide in the first place. However, keep in mind, this is one factor among several and varies by state. End-to-End Money Flow Here’s the simplest way to think about it. A customer pays your business. The payment lands in your business bank account. You use that account to pay for expenses like software subscriptions, contractor payments, or inventory. Whatever remains is your profit. Then, you set aside a portion of that profit for taxes. A good business bank account makes each of these steps easier to track, often with sub-accounts or tagging tools built in specifically for that purpose. How to Choose the Right Business Bank Account Business bank accounts can look almost identical on paper until you start using them. The differences show up in the details: transaction limits, integrations, fees, and features that match your stage of growth. Let’s break them down. Based on Your Business Type Freelancers and solopreneurs generally want low (or no) fees and simple interfaces, since they’re not managing payroll or multiple team cards. Startups need accounts that support investor reporting, cap table tools, and eventually payroll integrations. E-commerce businesses benefit most from accounts with strong Stripe, Amazon, or Shopify integrations and cash back on inventory and ad spend. Based on Transaction Volume If you’re processing a high volume of transactions, check whether the account caps free transactions per month or charges per-transaction fees beyond a certain threshold. Many online-first accounts advertise “unlimited” transactions, but it’s worth confirming this applies to ACH, wires, and card payments, not just one type. Based on Fees & Cost Structure Most online business banking platforms now charge $0 in monthly fees, a significant shift from a few years ago when even basic business checking carried a monthly charge. Don’t focus only on the headline fee. Pay close attention to minimum balance requirements. Check wire transfer costs, too. Also, see what happens to your fee structure if your balance falls below the required threshold. Best Bank Accounts for Small Businesses We’ve compared some of the best business bank accounts based on what they do best, from managing everyday expenses to supporting international payments and fast-growing businesses. Slash: Best for Spend Management & Growing Businesses Monthly fees: $0 on the Free plan Minimum balance: None Slash combines business banking , corporate cards, and spend management into a single platform, making it especially appealing for fast-growing startups and small businesses. With built-in expense controls, generous cashback, and deep accounting integrations, it helps entrepreneurs manage cash flow and team spending without juggling multiple tools. Key features: FDIC coverage up to hundreds of millions through partner bank Column N.A.’s sweep network, unlimited virtual cards with granular spend controls, up to 2% cashback with no caps, free domestic wires and ACH on qualifying plans, direct integrations with QuickBooks, Xero, and NetSuite Pros: No monthly fees or minimum balance on the core plan Cashback with no spending caps or bonus categories to track Strong spend controls, letting you set vendor-specific limits and get alerts on unauthorized activity Fast setup, with most accounts verified and ready to use the same day Cons: International wires carry a flat $25 fee Lending products run through credit partners rather than Slash directly, so approval timelines vary Why choose this? Slash is doola’s banking partner, which means it’s built to work seamlessly with the formation and compliance setup you’re already handling through doola. If you want banking, cards, and cash flow visibility in one dashboard without monthly fees, Slash is one of the strongest fits for a growing small business. Mercury: Best for Startups, SaaS companies, & US LLCs Monthly fees: $0 Minimum balance: None Mercury is one of the most popular fintech platforms for startups and LLCs, offering a clean, fee-free banking experience with modern financial tools. It’s particularly well-suited for entrepreneurs who want fast onboarding, strong integrations, and a scalable banking solution that grows with their business. Key features: Free domestic and international USD wires, API access, advanced user permissions, FDIC sweep coverage up to $5 million Pros: No monthly fees or minimum balance requirements Strong integrations for startups, including cap table and investor update tools Fast online approval, often within minutes once documents are submitted Cons: Doesn’t work with certain industries, including crypto and cannabis businesses No physical branches Tightened requirements mean it now generally expects a physical US address rather than a registered agent address Why choose this? If you want a single account that covers most small business needs without monthly costs, Mercury is the most well-rounded option on the market. Relay: For Low Fees & Budgeting Monthly fees: $0 on the Starter plan Minimum balance: None Relay is designed to simplify business budgeting by letting you create multiple checking accounts for different financial goals, such as taxes, payroll, and operating expenses. It’s an excellent choice for entrepreneurs who want better cash flow organization without paying monthly banking fees. Key features: Up to 20 individual checking accounts per business, up to 50 free Visa debit cards, cash back on card spend. Pros: No minimum balance or monthly maintenance fee Easiest platform for separating operating, tax, and profit funds Strong FDIC coverage through its banking partner Cons: No support for holding non-USD currencies Requires a physical US operating presence to qualify Why choose this? If staying organized matters more than any single feature, Relay’s sub-account structure does the budgeting work for you automatically. Novo: Best for E-Commerce Monthly fees: $0 Minimum balance: None Novo is built with online businesses in mind, offering seamless integrations with platforms like Shopify , Amazon, and Stripe to reduce manual financial admin. It’s streamlined banking experience makes it a strong fit for entrepreneurs running ecommerce brands or digital-first businesses. Key features: No fees on ACH transfers or incoming wires, ATM fee reimbursement up to $7 per month, built-in invoicing, direct Stripe integration . Pros: Designed specifically around e-commerce workflows Simple, fast online setup Some account tiers now offer interest on balances Cons: Requires beneficial owners to hold a US Social Security Number, which rules it out for many non-resident entrepreneurs Limited international wire support compared to multi-currency platforms Why choose this? If your business lives on Shopify or Amazon, Novo’s integrations remove a layer of manual reconciliation work. Lili: Best for Freelancers & Solopreneurs Monthly fees: $0 on the core plan Minimum balance: None Lili focuses on the needs of freelancers, contractors, and solo business owners by combining banking with built-in bookkeeping and tax tools. Its simple interface and self-employed-friendly features make it easy to separate business finances without unnecessary complexity. Key features: Built-in tax set aside calculator, expense tracking by category, access to working capital for eligible accounts Pros: Simple setup with minimal documentation required Tax tools built for self-employed income, not just generic business banking Doesn’t require a physical US address for some account types Cons: Fewer advanced tools for businesses with employees or high transaction volume Some premium features are excluded for non-US citizens Why choose this? If you’re a one-person business that just needs clean separation between personal and business money, Lili is built around exactly that use case. Wise Business: Best for International Payments Monthly fees: $0, though a small one-time setup fee may apply Minimum balance: None Wise Business specializes in helping companies send, receive, and manage money across borders with low foreign exchange fees and multi-currency accounts. It’s particularly valuable for businesses with international clients, contractors, or suppliers that want to avoid expensive traditional bank conversion rates. Key features: Hold and convert 40+ currencies, mid-market exchange rates, available in 170+ countries Pros: Among the easiest accounts for non-US residents to get approved for Significantly lower FX fees than most traditional banks Provides a real US routing and account number accepted by major payment processors Cons: Wise is a licensed money services business, not a bank. Your funds automatically receive FDIC pass-through insurance for up to 250,000 USD through their Program Bank Doesn’t build US business credit history the way a traditional bank relationship would Why choose this? If your business regularly sends or receives money across borders, Wise removes a meaningful chunk of the currency conversion cost. 🔖 Related Reading: 6 Wise Alternatives for Non-US Residents in 2026 Airwallex: Best for Global E-commerce Monthly fees: $0 on standard plans Minimum balance: None Airwallex is a global financial platform built for businesses operating across multiple countries and currencies. It combines multi-currency accounts, international payments, and foreign exchange tools into one solution, making it ideal for companies scaling globally. Key features: Multi-currency accounts in 20+ currencies, near-interbank FX rates, payments to 120+ countries Pros: Avoids forced currency conversion on incoming international payments Strong automation tools for global vendor payments Competitive option for entrepreneurs excluded from other platforms due to country restrictions Cons: More built for scaling global operations than simple domestic banking Onboarding documentation requirements can be more involved than domestic-first platforms Why choose this? If your customers or suppliers span multiple countries and currencies, Airwallex is built to handle that complexity without bleeding money on conversion fees. Bluevine: Best for Earning Interest Monthly fees: $0 on the standard checking plan Minimum balance: None Bluevine is a digital business banking platform that stands out by offering competitive interest on eligible checking balances alongside everyday business banking features. It’s a strong option for businesses that maintain higher cash reserves and want their idle funds to generate additional returns. Key features: Competitive APY on checking balances, line of credit options for qualifying businesses Pros: One of the stronger options for earning interest on a business checking balance No monthly fees or minimum balance requirements Cons: Fewer multi-account organizational tools compared to Relay Lending products require separate underwriting Why choose this? If you tend to keep a healthy cash buffer in your business account, Bluevine lets that balance work for you instead of sitting idle. Best Business Bank Accounts by Category ✔️ Best for Freelancers Lili leads here, with tax set aside tools and a setup process built around solo operators rather than teams. ✔️ Best for Startups Mercury remains the default for tech and SaaS entrepreneurs, particularly once investor reporting and payroll integrations come into play. If spend management and cashback matter more to you, Slash is a strong alternative , especially once you’re issuing cards to a growing team. ✔️ Best for E-Commerce Businesses Novo’s Stripe and Shopify integrations make it the strongest fit for online sellers managing inventory and ad spend. ✔️ Best for Low Fees Relay and Mercury both charge $0 per month with no minimum balance, making either a safe default if cost is your top priority. ✔️ Best for International Transactions Wise Business (formerly Transfer Wise) and Airwallex both outperform domestic-first banks on currency holding and FX rates, making them the clear picks if your business operates across borders. Key Features to Look for in a Business Bank Account Transaction Limits & Charges: Confirm whether ACH transfers, incoming wires, and debit transactions are genuinely unlimited or capped at a certain volume before fees kick in. A business processing hundreds of transactions a month can hit limits that a freelancer never will. Integrations with Accounting Tools: Look for direct integrations with bookkeeping software. An account that syncs automatically with your accounting tools saves hours of manual reconciliation every month. Online & Mobile Banking Experience: Since most of these accounts have no physical branches, the quality of the app and dashboard matters more than it would with a traditional bank. Check for mobile check deposit, real-time transaction alerts, and how easily you can issue cards to team members. Access to Credit & Financing: Some platforms offer lines of credit or working capital advances tied to your account history. If you anticipate needing financing down the line, banking with a provider that offers this can simplify approval since they have visibility into your cash flow. Customer Support Quality: Online-only banks vary widely in support responsiveness. If your business depends on fast resolution during a payment issue, read recent reviews specifically about support response times before committing. choose it for the wrong reasons. So, avoid these common pitfalls before opening your account to save time, money, and operational headaches as your business grows. Mistake Business Impact Solution Choosing based on brand recognition alone You could end up paying higher fees while getting fewer features than newer, business-focused banking platforms offer. Compare accounts based on the pricing, integrations, and business features and not just the bank’s name. Ignoring the fee structure until after signing up Monthly maintenance fees, wire fees, and other hidden charges can quietly reduce your profits over time. Review the full fee schedule upfront, including transfer fees, minimum balance requirements, and cash deposit costs. Not planning for scale As your business grows, switching bank accounts can be disruptive, requiring new account numbers, payment processor updates, and vendor changes. Choose a banking platform that can support your business as it adds customers, employees, and higher transaction volumes. Overlooking integrations Without built-in integrations for accounting software and payment processors, you’ll spend more time on manual reconciliation and increase the risk of errors. Prioritize accounts that integrate seamlessly with bookkeeping, invoicing, payroll, and payment tools. Real Example: Choosing the Right Bank Account Situation: An e-commerce entrepreneur selling on Shopify was using a personal checking account to manage business income, making tax season a multi-week cleanup project every year. Decision: She opened a dedicated business account with strong Shopify and Stripe integration , and used its automatic categorization tools to separate inventory spend, ad spend, and profit. Outcome: Bookkeeping that once took weeks dropped to just a few hours each month. She also had a much clearer picture of her finances. That made it easier to qualify for a small line of credit when she needed to restock inventory before a seasonal sales spike. What This Example Shows This business owner didn’t choose the account with the lowest fees or the biggest marketing claims. She chose the one that solved her biggest operational challenges. That’s exactly how you should evaluate your options. Is the “Best” Bank Account the Same for Every Business? No, your revenue stage matters: an early-stage solo entrepreneur has different needs than a business with five employees. Your business type matters: a service-based agency rarely needs the inventory-focused tools an e-commerce account offers. And your growth plans matter: an account that’s perfect today might not support payroll or multi-currency needs you’ll have in a year. There is no one-size-fits-all best business bank account. There’s only the account that fits where your business is now and where it’s headed next. Verdict: Which Business Bank Account Should You Choose? If you want a dependable, no-fee account that works for most small businesses, Mercury is the safest starting point. The right choice isn’t about finding the single “best” bank, it’s about matching the account to how your business actually operates. Freelancers and solo operators are usually better served by Lili’s simpler, tax-focused setup. E-commerce sellers should lean toward Novo for its native integrations, and any business with international customers or vendors should strongly consider pairing a domestic account with Wise Business or Airwallex to avoid unnecessary FX costs. body_text: MONTREAL , July 17, 2026 /CNW/ -- (NYSE: CAE) (TSX: CAE ) CAE and Saab today announced the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to collaborate on advanced training, simulation, and mission support capabilities for the Gripen fighter aircraft in Canada should the Government of Canada choose to make the Gripen part of its future fighter capability. Under the proposed collaboration, CAE would play a key role in establishing and operating a Canadian-based training ecosystem for Gripen pilots and technicians, supporting advanced pilot training, simulator operations, technical training, and sustainment services. CAE and Saab would also explore opportunities to support mission systems development and sustainment in Canada, combining Saab's platform expertise with CAE's world-class training, simulation, and operational support solutions. "This agreement reflects a shared commitment to supporting Canada's long-term defence readiness, and we're proud to serve Canada's men and women in uniform through world-class training, simulation, and mission systems support," said Matthew Bromberg, CAE President and CEO. "Our collaboration with Saab can help strengthen Canada's future fighter capability while creating meaningful opportunities for Canadian engineers, technicians, and aviation professionals." "Saab's approach has always been to build real capability in the countries where we operate," said Micael Johansson, CEO of Saab. "Through this partnership with CAE, we would establish a world-class training and mission support capability in Canada, creating highly skilled jobs while ensuring critical knowledge, expertise, and operational data remain in Canadian hands." The agreement includes collaboration on research and development initiatives focused on next-generation capabilities, reinforcing a shared commitment to innovation, operational effectiveness, and long-term readiness. In addition to supporting potential future Gripen capabilities in Canada, the MoU opens opportunities for CAE and Saab to explore collaboration on Gripen-related training, mission support, and sustainment opportunities in international markets. About CAE At CAE , we exist to make the world safer. We deliver cutting-edge training, simulation, and critical operations solutions to prepare aviation professionals and defence forces for the moments that matter. Every day, we empower pilots, cabin crew, maintenance technicians, airlines, business aviation operators, and defence and security personnel to perform at their best and when the stakes are the highest. Around the globe, we're everywhere customers need us to be with sites and training locations in over 40 countries. For nearly 80 years, CAE has been at the forefront of innovation, consistently seeking to set the standard by delivering excellence in high-fidelity flight simulators and training solutions, while embedding sustainability at the heart of everything we do. By harnessing technology and enhancing human performance, we strive to be the trusted partner in advancing safety and mission readiness - today and tomorrow.
